title: Why Is Garajau Named After a Seabird?
description: Garajau is the Madeiran word for the common tern, a seabird nesting on the cliffs from spring to autumn. The headland, statue and reserve that share its name.
heroAlt: A common tern hovering over the sea below the brown cliffs of Ponta do Garajau
keywords: why is garajau named after a seabird

images.prompt: Early afternoon in June off the south-east coast of Madeira near Ponta do Garajau, seen from the water. In sharp focus, a single common tern hovers about two metres above a calm, deep blue sea, wings raised, forked tail spread, black cap and red bill clearly visible, looking down for a fish. Behind it, out of focus, the steep brown and green cliffs of the Garajau headland with a small white statue far away on top. Bright natural light, true colours, realistic wildlife photo, no text.
images.alt: A common tern hovering over the sea below the brown cliffs of Ponta do Garajau
